static_traits.name: Lin Hao
static_traits.social_status: Impaired self-esteem lowering social willingness, avoiding dining out with friends; can chat daily with roommates but unwilling to share inferiority feelings
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problem history before; not yet received counseling or treatment
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, can describe emotions and behaviors; negative-leaning thinking, self-deprecation, tending to negate positive feedback; skeptical about change but willing to try, acceptable cooperativeness, overall negative tone

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling 'boring, uninteresting, and terrible' for liking eating macaroni and cheese, affecting self-perception and self-esteem, then avoiding socializing and trying new activities.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because I noticed this inferiority limits my social interactions and overall enjoyment of life.
growth_experiences: About a year ago, under the ongoing influence of social media and public opinion, gradually internalized the value standard that 'being unique and daring to try counts as interesting / cool'; when eating macaroni and cheese or seeing others try a variety of foods, feeling inferior and ashamed, then reducing dining out with friends, having tried new foods and activities but still negating positive feedback, the problem gradually worsening and affecting daily life and socializing.

core_beliefs: I am a boring, childish, unattractive person
My value depends on others' evaluations and whether I am sufficiently 'different / daring to try'

special_situations.event: When dining alone or with others, chooses macaroni and cheese
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my food preferences are not diverse or 'adventurous' enough, it means I am boring and not worthy of recognition
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-criticism, forcing herself to try new foods to prove she is 'not a boring person'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Eating like this is too childish, too uninteresting

special_situations.event: Sees others trying diverse foods or social media praise for 'adventurous eating'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others are more 'diverse / unique', they are better than me and more worthy of attention
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Compares and demeans himself on social media, reduces eating out with others
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Others are all more interesting than me, and their lives are better than mine too

special_situations.event: Others' positive feedback on one's trying new foods or efforts
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If praise is small or comes from acquaintances, it does not count, not credible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive feedback, thinking the other is just being polite
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite, not really thinking this

special_situations.event: Plans to dine out with friends or thinks about possibly being seen by others making my dietary choices
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I order by my own taste, others will look down on me, mock me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding eating out with friends,Reduced socializing
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am very childish, very boring

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be accepted, seen as valuable and 'interesting', to live by her own preferences without being shamed
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being mocked, belittled, and labeled 'childish / boring', thus being rejected or excluded
defense_goal: Reducing chances of being judged by avoiding socializing
Avoiding hope-and-disappointment swings by negating others' positive feedback
Preemptive self-deprecation to reduce the impact when humiliated

object_relations.self_representation: A boring, not-good-enough person being judged
object_relations.object_representation: Harsh, comparison-loving judges or superior peers / the public

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor gives affirmation or emphasizes one's positive efforts (such as being willing to try self-compassion)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing others' affirmation is 'not sincere, just politeness', hard to accept positive feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Downplaying or dissecting compliments, responding with 'this is nothing / just politeness', reserved tone, avoiding emotional investment.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing how others may view their eating preferences or performance in social settings
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Projecting the inner self-criticism experience as 'others will look down on me / think I am childish'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Stating 'they will mock me' in a certain tone, not actively seeking evidence, with tension and avoidance.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor encourages trying new cognitive or self-compassion practices
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Refusing to try on the grounds that 'this is fake / useless to me', thereby maintaining existing beliefs
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gives reasons in a calm but skeptical tone (such as 'it feels fake') to politely decline the exercise, reducing emotional involvement.

manifestations: Personal preferences swayed by social media and social standards
Repressing true preferences to meet the external 'interesting / cool' standard
outcomes: Rising anxiety and avoiding social situations

manifestations: Unwilling to discuss inferiority and inadequacy with roommates
outcomes: Reduced social ties, limited available support

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Takes the social standard that 'daring to try novel foods counts as interesting/cool' as the sole basis for self-evaluation
Reproaching herself with inner language like 'should / must try better'

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Presuming others will ridicule one's dietary preferences ('they will think I am childish')
Projecting the self-criticism experience as the outside world's negative evaluation

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Highly self-reproaching, repeatedly comparing and negating herself
Staying skeptical of others' praise and quickly negating its validity

positive_force: Stable work performance; has a basic daily routine
Can be self-aware of problems and actively seeks help
Shows a certain willingness to try in counseling (despite having doubts)
Having a daily supportive relationship foundation (lives with roommates)
negative_force: Excessively concerned about outside evaluations and internalizes social media standards
Avoiding socializing and dining out, reinforcing negative beliefs
Negating positive feedback, hard to integrate positive experiences

antecedent: Thinking about ordering macaroni and cheese for oneself
Seeing others try a variety of foods
Scrolling to social media praise of 'adventurous eating'
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalizing the standard that 'only diverse / adventurous is valuable', fearing being judged childish and boring, triggering shame and anxiety
target_behavior.function: Escaping being evaluated and shame, gaining a short-term sense of safety
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced socializing, rising loneliness, decreased enjoyment of life, maintaining negative self-perception

target_behavior.behavior: Negating others' positive feedback ('they are just polite')
antecedent: Others' praise/approval of one's trying new foods or efforts
The counselor's positive reflection and encouragement
target_behavior.core_reason: Maintaining the existing schema of 'I am very boring / not good enough' to avoid the pain of dashed expectations
target_behavior.function: Maintains cognitive consistency; reduces emotional vulnerability
target_behavior.consequence: Hard to integrate positive experiences, self-esteem unable to rise, negative emotions persisting

target_behavior.behavior: Self-deprecating negative self-talk (such as 'I am childish/terrible')
antecedent: Sees others' varied diets or social media content
Thinking about sharing a meal with others
target_behavior.core_reason: Equating individual preferences with overall human worth in all-or-nothing terms, overgeneralizing own flaws
target_behavior.function: Through preemptive self-criticism, tries to control the emotional impact when humiliated by others
target_behavior.consequence: Intensified shame and anxiety, further avoiding socializing and lowering life satisfaction
